rationale: Executing the registered discriminator for the restore-on-monotonic-store reachability question. The harness builds a real single-node cluster over the test monotonic log store with default TrailingLogs and a shortened SnapshotInterval, takes an internal snapshot, opens it and burns the index upward, then calls the production Restore and samples the store's last index, the cached snapshot index, the applied index, the number of stored snapshots and shouldSnapshot before the restore, immediately after it, and after more than one snapshot interval. Native construction feedback with those fixed inputs gave a NEGATIVE result that constrains the earlier claim: before the restore store_last=3/snapshot_index=3/should_snapshot=false; after the restore store_last=105, snapshot_index=104, applied=105, should_snapshot=false (so the store was not emptied and the trigger did not fire); after the interval the snapshot count was unchanged at 2 and should_snapshot stayed false. The likely source of the difference is that the Restore API appends a trailing noop entry after the restore, which leaves one log entry above the snapshot index and keeps the delta small. This submission records the fixed experiment for controller execution; the measured interpretation and any narrowing of the asserted defect's limitations are left for the retained receipt.

scope.description: One process, one real single-node cluster built over the test monotonic log store with default TrailingLogs/SnapshotThreshold and SnapshotInterval shortened to 150ms. The node applies one command, takes an internal snapshot, opens it and raises its index by 100, then runs the production Restore. Store last index, cached snapshot index, applied index, stored-snapshot count and shouldSnapshot are recorded before the restore, immediately after it, and after 700ms (more than four intervals).

experiment.prefix: The cluster is created with the snapshot helper's custom constructor using Peers=1, Bootstrap=true and MonotonicLogs=true, so the node's log store is the test monotonic wrapper over InmemStore and IsMonotonic is genuinely true; the same log store is passed to BootstrapCluster. The restore input is produced by the target's own Snapshot() future and Open(), with only meta.Index adjusted upward as the existing restore tests do, so the payload and metadata stay the target's own. No production logic is modified; observations are package-internal reads of the runtime object plus the snapshot store's List().
